text:
ashley: Ok team — planning thread for long-term routing + multi-region + multi-tenant isolation roadmap. Need to reconcile three customer-driven asks and agree launch criteria for Q3/Q4. cc @pavan @tess :eyes:

pavan: quick summary of asks: FinCorp needs <50ms tail latency in EU + NA, EduScale needs strict data residency (EU only), Platform wants tenant slicing for noisy neighbors.

tess: propose we break into three initiatives: 1) Policy DSL + guardrails, 2) Region affinity + traffic steering, 3) Tenant slices + soft-eviction. Each with explicit launch gates.

sam: can we get rough estimates? small/med/large? also flag infra blockers (cross-region bandwidth, db replication).

lina: gating ideas: must have canary with two customers, automated fallback to lower-cost model, and regression evals on prompt-set (~1000 queries). Also cap on monthly cost delta <= 10% for hosted customers.

pavan: tradeoffs: policy DSL gives us runtime flexibility but is ~6-8w dev + 4w ops. Region affinity is mostly infra (routing fabric) ~8w + networking approvals. Tenant slices requires scheduler + admission controls, estimate ~10-12w.

ashley: thanks. For launch criteria draft: - SLA: p95 latency target per region (FinCorp: p95 <50ms) - Isolation: noisy-tenant mitigation validated under 3x baseline load - DR/residency: traffic routes and audit logs proving EU-only for EduScale - Observability: per-tenant cost/latency dashboards - Rollout: pilot (1 hosted, 1 dedicated) then 3-week canary - Cost guardrail: <10% unit cost uplift or rollback.

sam: got it. Any preference on sequencing? my read: policy DSL first because it unlocks safe rollout for the rest.

tess: agree on DSL first, but we should parallelize small infra spikes for region affinity to avoid a long linear timeline.

pavan: quick policy example (very rough):
```
policy {
  match tenant: "edu-scale/*"
  route region_preference: ["eu-west-1"]
  fallback: "hosted-quantized-v2"
  isolation: {max_tokens_per_min: 10000}
}
```

ashley: nice. add to spec doc. also need RICE-style prioritization from product and an internal cost delta estimate from infra.

lina: for gating we should add an automated rollback trigger: if error-rate > 1% or tail-latency increase > 20% for 15m, autoswitch to fallback.

sam: question: dedicated vs hosted commit model impacts rollout speed. Dedicated customers can be pilot first. ask sales to surface willing pilots.

ashley: action items: 1) @pavan create spec PR with DSL + example policies (due EOD Thu) 2) @tess run infra spike plan for cross-region steering (estimate + blockers) 3) @sam coordinate with sales for pilot candidates 4) @lina define regression / rollback tests and alert thresholds. I'll assemble RICE scoring by Friday.

ashley: also negotiate scope with stakeholders: if customer SLAs force heavy infra changes, we may scope to 'paid dedicated' first and delay hosted default. call this out in the spec.

dev-bot: RFC created: https://rfc.redwood.local/r/long-term-routing-2026 (status: draft) :page_facing_up:

ashley: perfect — if folks can drop updates in the RFC and ping here, we'll lock priorities at next product sync. :thumbsup:
